To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The cellularity of the spleen and submaxillary lymph node, the percentage of lymphocytes expressing the CD4, CD8 and double-positive (DP) markers, and the LPS- and Con A-induced lymphocyte proliferation are different during the light and dark phases.
the circadian rhythm of the immune system is different in the submaxillar lymph nodes and spleens of adult male mice and is modulated by timed administration of prolactin.
The circadian variation of the immune response in the submaxillar lymph nodes and spleens of adult male mice was investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of timed administration of h-Prolactin (hPRL) on the cellularity, lymphocyte subpopulations, blastogenic proliferation induced by Concanavalin A and Lipopolysaccharides (LPS) and Natural Killer (NK) activity in the submaxillar lymph nodes and spleens of adult male mice.
the effects of light/dark recombinant human PRL administration on the immune response of submaxillary lymph node and spleen in adult male mice.
the circadian variations in immune function and the differential effects of h-PRL administration on the immune response of the submaxillary glands and spleen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the administration of hPRL during the dark period induces immunosuppression and during the light period immunostimulation in the spleen and submaxillary lymph node, respectively.
the effects of h-PRL administration are dependent on the phase in which it is administered.
the circadian variations of the immune system and the effects of h-PRL on these circadian variations are not the same in the two lymphoid organs investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immune system has a circadian rhythm that can be influenced by h-PRL.
the circadian variation in the cellular immune function in the lymphoid organs is dependent upon the lymphoid structure considered.
prolactin is an immunomodulator, and that this effect is dependent upon the time of day when it is administered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the circadian rhythm of the immune system can be modulated by exogenous factors.
the immune system is not static, but is constantly changing in response to the external and internal environment.
the circadian rhythm is a key regulator of immune function.
